titleEn: See Smoke? Go to the Water!

pages.text: "Roots! Yum!" Tumba dug in the dry grassland. Moya grazed beside them. Tumba wanted more sweet roots, so they dug and dug.
Moya sniffed. "Tumba, look. The sky's hazy." Smoke rose at the far edge of the field. "Just a little more! There are roots left!" Tumba didn't look up.
The wind brought a sharp smell. Cough! Tumba looked up at last. "What's that?" The smoke had grown. Startled, Tumba looked around, unsure what to do.
Mom ran over and spoke calmly. "It's a grassland fire. Still far away. Come to the water with me." Her voice helped Tumba settle. They left the roots and followed her.

All three stood on wet dirt at the waterhole's edge. "When there's smoke, the water's edge is safest," Mom said. "No dry grass here for the fire to follow." Tumba pressed a hoof into the cool, damp ground.
Mom whispered, "Let's pretend to be hippos. A hippo resting on its tummy by the water isn't afraid." Tumba pictured a huge hippo in the water, then lay flat. "I'm a hippo!"
Mom taught three promises. "One, see smoke—stop digging! Two, follow a grown-up to the water! Three, stay close there!" Tumba and Moya nodded and called, "See smoke? Go to the water!"
Smoke drifted away in the distance and the sky turned blue again. All three watched quietly, lying by the water. With Mom there, they weren't afraid. Tumba's tail popped up. "We kept every promise!"
Tumba knew all three promises now. "One, stop digging at smoke! Two, follow a grown-up to the water! Three, stay close!" They lifted their snout and called loudly, "See smoke? Go to the water!"

Mom held Tumba and Moya at either side and nuzzled them. "You both stayed calm and kept the promises!" They had stopped what they were doing and gone to the water when they saw smoke. See smoke? Go to the water!
